items.title: two ADMITTED impl blocks providing one trait DEFAULT with different trait arguments — `impl Box with Counting<i32> {}` beside `impl Box with Counting<str> {}` — are ONE candidate for `box.next()` and `for item in box`, the first block registered: `inherited_default_candidates` dedups by member id after the admission narrowing, so the loop's item is `i32` or `str` by the modules' load order, where `rank_member_candidates`' homes rule (B73 R1) calls the same pair ambiguous

items.body: Repro: `sweeps/order49/incr-49/finds/default_next_two_homes/` — `first_i32/` and `first_str/` are one program whose two impl modules are named so their load order reverses; `vilan check .` is clean in the first (`item` is `i32`) and refused in the second (`let copy: i32 = item`: `item` is `str`). `inherited_default_candidates` (analyzer.rs, after the B401 narrowing) collapses candidates by MEMBER id — the trait's one `next` — so two admitted homes with different trait arguments are one candidate, the first in `implementations`; the permutation differential's `m128_for_each` fixture holds the declined/admitted shape (fixed by M128: the loop's lookup is admitted under the looping file, the provider stored by block id), and this both-admitted shape is its residue. Rec: key the dedup on (member, home arguments) as `rank_member_candidates` keys a home, and report the pair as ambiguous at the loop/call; add the both-admitted state to the `m128_for_each` fixture when it holds. Sizing S; solver.
